candidates.section_title: Affine charts for flag Hilbert schemes

candidates.statement: The fact that the open sets of Definition [\[def:chart\]](#def:chart){reference-type="ref" reference="def:chart"} cover the whole of $\mathrm{FHilb}_n$ follows from the following principle: $$\label{eqn:principletorus} \textbf{any open torus invariant property which holds}$$ $$\textbf{near the fixed points of }\mathrm{FHilb}_n \textbf{ holds everywhere}$$ This is because the set of points which do not enjoy said property is closed, torus invariant and contains no fixed points: any such set must be empty.
One must be careful here, because the argument is a priori only true for projective varieties, such as $\mathrm{FHilb}_n(\mathrm{point})$.

If we are in the case $* = \mathbb{C}$ or $* = \mathrm{point}$, then we must set $y_i^i = 0$ or $x_i^i = y_i^i = 0$ in [\[eqn:chartx\]](#eqn:chartx){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:chartx"} and [\[eqn:charty\]](#eqn:charty){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:charty"}, respectively.
The only basis vectors which remain unsolved for should be the ones that appear in the codomain of [\[eqn:zzzz\]](#eqn:zzzz){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:zzzz"}.
To compute the full endomorphism ring of the projector $P_T$, we should tensor with $\wedge^{\bullet}\mathcal{T}_n^{\vee}$.

In particular, Conjecture [\[conj:homfly\]](#conj:homfly){reference-type="ref" reference="conj:homfly"} implies that $\mathrm{End}(P_T)$ should be the tensor product of the homology on the "bottom row" with an exterior algebra.

Our main Example [\[ex:proj dg\]](#ex:proj dg){reference-type="ref" reference="ex:proj dg"} should be interpreted as a dg version of the familiar notion of projective bundles $\mathrm{Proj}\ S_X\mathcal{V}\stackrel{\pi}\longrightarrow X$, where $\mathcal{V}$ is a rank $n$ locally free sheaf of $X$.
